question.text: A capacitor has capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> when its parallel plates are separated by air medium of thickness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math>. A slab of material of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> having area equal to that of plates but thickness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> is inserted between the plates. Capacitance of the capacitor in the presence of slab will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor when air is present C=ϵ0Ad=5 μF

After insertion of dielectric, the equivalent capacitance of the new capacitor is 

Ceq=ϵ0 Ad21.5+d21

=ε0 Ad3+d2=6ε0 A5d

=65×5 μF=6 μF.
